record.paper_title: Whitehead's Asphericity Question and Its Relation to Other Open Problems
record.original_question: If a group G has cohomological dimension 2, must G admit a two-dimensional Eilenberg-MacLane complex K(G,1)?

evidence.quote: every group G with cdG = 2 has a two-dimensional K (G, 1)-complex

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a discrete group. The cohomological dimension of $G$, denoted $\operatorname{cd}(G)$, is the supremum of integers $n$ such that $H^n(G; M) \neq 0$ for some $\mathbb{Z}G$-module $M$. An Eilenberg–MacLane complex $K(G,1)$ is a connected CW complex with fundamental group $G$ and contractible universal cover; its dimension is the dimension of the underlying CW complex.

Question: If $G$ is a group with $\operatorname{cd}(G) = 2$, must there exist a 2-dimensional CW complex that is a $K(G,1)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture (1957), which remains an open problem. It is known that any group of cohomological dimension 2 admits a 3-dimensional $K(G,1)$. Bestvina and Brady (1997) constructed groups providing potential counterexamples, showing that at least one of the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture and the Whitehead asphericity conjecture must fail, but neither has been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In 1997, Mladen Bestvina and Noel Brady constructed a group G so that either G is a counterexample to the Eilenberg–Ganea conjecture, or there must be a counterexample to the Whitehead conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture remains unresolved; only conditional results are known.

status_evidence.snippet: Listed among unsolved problems in low-dimensional topology.
